race_context: Beech Grove City Schools (legally the School City of Beech Grove) serves Beech Grove on Indianapolis' southeast side in Marion County {cb_bg_2026}{dlgf_bg_det}. It runs Beech Grove High School, Beech Grove Middle School, Central Intermediate, South Grove Elementary, Hornet Park Elementary, Hornet Park Early Childhood Center and K-12 virtual programs {bg_board}. State counts show enrollment of 2,790 in 2024-25 and 5,481 in 2025-26; Chalkbeat described it in 2026 as a district of 'nearly 5,500 students,' up from about 3,000 in its 2022 and 2024 guides {idoe_enroll}{cb_bg_2026}{cb_bg_2022}{cb_bg_2024}.
Superintendent: Dr. Laura Hammack, hired by a unanimous board vote in 2021 {bg_ref}{cb_bg_2022}.

The board has seven members elected at large, so every voter in the district may vote for every open seat; terms are four years {cb_bg_2022}{cb_bg_2024}. Current members listed by the district: Jannis King (president), Tara Wolf (vice president), April Rinks (secretary), Beth Prindle, Brian Downard, Jill Laker and Madison West {bg_board}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: three at-large seats, not one as the state list's 'vote for 1' suggests {cb_bg_2026}{in_list}. These are the seats won unopposed in 2022 by Rob Challis, Jannis King and Rick Skirvin {cb_bg_2022}. Downard was appointed in January 2024 to the vacancy left by Skirvin, and West was appointed in July 2026 to the seat vacated by Challis {cb_bg_2026}. All three current holders are running and are unopposed, so all three will be elected {cb_bg_2026}{cb_mc_2026}. Winners serve from January 2027 through December 2030 {cb_bg_2026}{cb_mc_2026}.

Party labels: 2026 is the first year Indiana school board candidates could list a party; King is running as an Independent, while Downard and West did not declare a party {cb_bg_2026}{cb_mc_2026}{in_list}.

Operating referendum (Nov. 3, 2026): on June 17, 2026 the board approved putting an operating referendum on the ballot to replace the one voters approved in 2020 {govly_jun17}{bg_ref}. The state-approved ballot question asks for a rate of up to 57 cents per $100 of assessed value, raising up to $4.4 million a year for up to eight years, for school bus transportation, facilities maintenance and student safety including school resource officers {dlgf_bg_det}. The question states that a median $200,000 home's tax bill would rise $493 a year {dlgf_bg_det}. The district says that because it replaces the 2020 levy, the median homeowner would pay slightly less than now (about $6.76 less in 2027) {bg_ref}; WRTV reported district documents showing an average increase of $1.25 a month {wrtv_ref}.

Budget and SEA 1: Hammack told WRTV that the operations fund, which pays for transportation, utilities, maintenance, custodial services and school safety, is strained by property tax caps and that SEA 1 will reduce revenue as assessed values decline; the district expects about $4 million in annual cuts if the referendum fails {wrtv_ref}. A third-party summary of the July 15, 2026 meeting says the board voted to advertise the 2027 budget and reviewed transportation-lot security upgrades and an energy audit {govly_jul15}.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum. Chalkbeat Indiana, Mirror Indy and WFYI published a candidate survey; Downard and West answered and King did not respond {cb_bg_2026}. Both respondents said they support the referendum {cb_bg_2026}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent, appointed in January 2024; running unopposed for one of three at-large seats {cb_bg_2026}.
background: Works in aerospace engineering and has two children in Beech Grove schools {cb_bg_2026}.
Appointed to the board in January 2024 to fill the vacancy left by longtime member Rick Skirvin {cb_bg_2026}.
path_to_ballot: On the ballot without a party label; Chalkbeat reported he did not declare a party affiliation {in_list}{cb_bg_2026}.

items: Told Chalkbeat the district faces 'overwhelming impacts from the legislation and tax base,' has been 'doing more with less' and has an 'extremely thin budget' {cb_bg_2026}.
Said he 'absolutely support[s] the 2026 operating referendum,' saying the rate was designed to 'limit impact to our taxpayers,' and committed to asking only for what is needed {cb_bg_2026}.

Lists 'educational quality, academic experience, safety, and well-being' of students as priorities; said foundational literacy and math matter and that his focus is STEM and students' 'vocational callings' {cb_bg_2026}.
Said he is 'always willing to discuss any topic' and welcomes feedback on how to represent the community {cb_bg_2026}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. He described his immediate focus as passing the 2026 operating referendum and continuing to improve operational efficiency {cb_bg_2026}.
plans: Pass the operating referendum and keep improving operational efficiency; expand STEM opportunities {cb_bg_2026}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: No campaign website, social media page or forum remarks were found.
Marion County campaign finance filings were not checked.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board president, on the board for more than a decade; running unopposed as an Independent {cb_bg_2026}{bg_board}.
background: Board president, on the board for more than a decade {cb_bg_2026}{bg_board}.

In 2022 Chalkbeat reported she worked as a part-time substitute teacher through Kelly Services and served as the school board's ex-officio appointee on the Beech Grove Parks and Recreation Board {cb_bg_2022}.
Was re-elected unopposed in 2022 and was among the members who unanimously hired Superintendent Laura Hammack in 2021 {cb_bg_2022}.
path_to_ballot: Listed as an Independent on the state candidate list {in_list}{cb_bg_2026}.
on_incumbent: Is a current board member and its president. She did not respond to multiple requests to complete the 2026 Chalkbeat/Mirror Indy/WFYI candidate survey, and no statement from her on the board's record was found {cb_bg_2026}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: No 2026 campaign statements, website, questionnaire answers or forum remarks were found; her positions are unknown.
Marion County campaign finance filings were not checked.

candidates.summary: Incumbent, appointed in July 2026; running unopposed for one of three at-large seats {cb_bg_2026}.
background: Works in government affairs and has three young children in the district {cb_bg_2026}.
Appointed in July 2026 to the seat vacated by Rob Challis; a third-party summary of the July 15, 2026 meeting says she was sworn in that night {cb_bg_2026}{govly_jul15}.
path_to_ballot: On the ballot without a party label; Chalkbeat reported she did not declare a party affiliation {in_list}{cb_bg_2026}.

items: Named long-term financial stability as the most pressing issue, calling the referendum 'an important short-term solution' and saying the district needs a 'sustainable, long-term funding model' {cb_bg_2026}.

Supports the 57-cent referendum, calling it a 'fiscally responsible step'; said 'affordability and fiscal responsibility must remain top priorities' and that she would advocate for funding at the state level {cb_bg_2026}.
Wants to strengthen early literacy, support growth at every grade, and build pathways to college, careers and skilled trades {cb_bg_2026}.
Said 'effective leadership begins with listening' and plans to attend school and community events {cb_bg_2026}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member (since July 2026). She described the referendum as providing 'critical funding needed to maintain the high-quality education our students deserve' {cb_bg_2026}.
plans: Support the referendum, seek a long-term funding model, and focus on early literacy and career pathways {cb_bg_2026}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found.
gaps: No campaign website, social media page or forum remarks were found.
Her employer in government affairs was not identified.
The departing member's name appears as 'Rob Challis' (Chalkbeat) and 'Rob Chalice' (a third-party meeting summary); official minutes were not checked.
Marion County campaign finance filings were not checked.
